_how_to_fill_this_in: One object per requirement. Fill in every field; replace every '…'. Do not rename the fields.

id: REQ-001, REQ-002 … in order. Ids never change after this week: the chain requirement → use case → screen → test case → api.md row points at them. A requirement you drop keeps its id and gets 'dropped': true.
This file is the only place for the requirements. Do not copy them into SRS.md: SRS §4 and §5 hold one line, 'The requirements are in week02/requirements.json.'
description: one sentence, one behaviour, something you could test. Not 'the app is user-friendly'; 'a student books a free slot of 30 to 120 minutes'.
functional: true if it says WHAT the system does (a user can…, the system sends…); false if it says HOW WELL (speed, security, privacy, capacity, phone screen, language).
priority: must (the product is pointless without it — ships in Week 11), should (important, cut only if time runs out), could (nice to have). Not everything is a must: that is the point of the field.

acceptance: the test that proves the requirement is met — what you do and what you must see. From Week 4 it becomes a test case that you really run. Example: 'Enter the code from the e-mail within 10 minutes: logged in. Three wrong codes in a row: locked for 15 minutes.'

At least 8: at least 5 functional and at least 3 non-functional. REQ-001 (login) and REQ-006 (phone screen) are the same for everyone; adjust the wording to your product. The login rules are fixed: a 4-digit code sent by e-mail, valid for 10 minutes, works once; a new code within 60 seconds → 429; 3 wrong codes in a row → the address is locked for 15 minutes (429); no passwords; no social login.

Change requests: from the Sunday after Week 5 (the baseline), every change to this file, a dropped requirement included, is a change request: one line in the Change log of PROPOSAL.md that begins with CR- and the next number, names the change and the ids, and lists every file it affects. Example: '2026-10-28 — CR-01: REQ-002 now allows 15-minute slots; affects requirements.json, test_cases.json (TC-002-02), week05/api.md, server/bookings.py.'
You may delete this _how_to_fill_this_in block once you have read it; the checker ignores it.

requirements.description: A new user signs up with an e-mail address and logs in with the 4-digit code sent to it; no passwords and no social login.
requirements.acceptance: The 4-digit code arrives by e-mail within one minute; entering it within 10 minutes logs the user in, and it works only once; an expired or wrong code is refused with a message; a new code asked within 60 seconds is refused (429); 3 wrong codes in a row lock the address for 15 minutes (429).

requirements.description: Every screen is usable on a phone about 390 px wide without horizontal scrolling.
requirements.acceptance: Every screen opened on a 390 px wide phone (or the browser's phone view): no horizontal scroll bar, no text cut off, every button reachable.
